evidence.title: Steiner, Caffrey and Barth, Coalescence of Designed and Natural Space Radiological Environments
evidence.location: NASA/TM-20250006822, printed pp 9,11; PDF pp 13,15; Figures 8,10
evidence.finding: Matched annual Si dose curves, solid Al spheres, solar maximum, source 95% confidence. Fig 8 integral flux above LET after 100 mil Al. Lunar-surface text gives 2.17 krad(Si)/year at 100 mil.
evidence.conditions: SPENVIS SEP inputs, IRENE belts, FASTRAD dose; specific submodel versions, epoch and spectrum files not supplied. 550 km/6 deg and 800 km/98 deg LEO. Interplanetary proxy for distant lunar observer.
evidence.limits: Digitization adds +/-15% reading allowance, not a statistical CI. Source 95% cannot be recalculated from published inputs. No new transport run. Lunar surface is not low lunar orbit. Do not adopt the report's p 8 SEP upper-energy wording: SEP can exceed GeV.
evidence.access: full PDF cached; figures visually checked

evidence.title: Mazur et al., New measurements of total ionizing dose in the lunar environment
evidence.location: Space Weather 9 S07002, doi:10.1029/2010SW000641; abstract; paras 16,22,39-40
evidence.finding: 12.2 rad(Si) in first 333 days; delayed solar-cycle rise with no intense SEP. 50 km lunar-orbit rate about 30% below interplanetary.
evidence.conditions: 2009-2010 solar minimum. Microdosimeter nominal attitude: lunar-facing minimum 0.89 g/cm 2 Al, space-facing 2.28 g/cm 2. Integrated history includes mission phases and gaps corrected in paper.
evidence.limits: 13.4 rad/year annualization is a quiet-era comparator, not solar-event design dose, and not the same shielding as RAD01. Do not divide the two as matched cases.
evidence.access: publisher full HTML read; PDF cache not obtained

evidence.title: Spence et al., Relative contributions of galactic cosmic rays and lunar proton albedo to dose and dose rates near the Moon
evidence.kind: validated transport interpretation of lunar measurements
evidence.finding: Reported modeled total dose rate in silicon 372 microGy/day. Primary GCR plus lunar secondary/albedo fields.
evidence.conditions: CRaTER-specific response, near-Moon geometry and selected GCR conditions; not a generic electronics shielding case.
evidence.limits: 13.6 rad/year arithmetic context only. Do not apply a universal half-sky factor to primary plus secondary dose.

evidence.title: Wilcox et al., Event-Based Vision Sensor Lifetime Degradation in Low Earth Orbit
evidence.location: Sensors 25,6599; doi:10.3390/s25216599; abstract; sections 1.2,3,4.1; PDF pp 1-3,15-16
evidence.finding: Two DAVIS240C sensors on ISS, Jan 2022-Sep 2024 data. One of 18 measures showed convincing deterioration; mild row/column error growth. Quarter-inch (6.35 mm) 6061 Al enclosure, open lens apertures.
evidence.conditions: Intermittent commanded acquisition, changing scenes and biases, ISS geomagnetic environment; not continuous monitoring or a measured per-device qualification dose.
evidence.limits: Encouraging technology heritage. Does not qualify IMX636, lunar radiation, faint-flash radiometry or optical transmission stability. Generic dose/sea-level ratio in discussion is not used here.
evidence.access: full publisher PDF cached; relevant pages checked

evidence.title: McMahon-Crabtree et al., Automated characterization techniques and testbeds for event-based cameras
evidence.finding: PPS3MVCD and DAVIS346 (180 nm) showed dose-dependent background activity and functional issues above about 30 krad. One DAVIS346 failed at 50 krad after 20 krad step. A proton-exposed DAVIS346 recovered after rest/power cycle. At 20 krad proton exposure, dark current rose about 70% and dark event noise 23% (filter off).
evidence.conditions: PPS3MVCD Co 60 dose rate 52.1 rad(Si)/s, multiple devices. DAVIS346 gamma 4.23 rad(Si)/s; separate 64 MeV proton test reaches 1.498e11 p/cm 2 at 20 krad. Targeted irradiation; packaged-camera support circuitry can confound attribution.
evidence.limits: Cross-technology and sample-limited comparator, not IMX636 tolerance. Proton test combines TID and DD; no isolated DD coefficient or flight-rate cross-section. High dose-rate results do not bound all low-dose-rate/annealing effects.
evidence.access: author-uploaded full text read on ResearchGate; PDF download403; exact table tokens recorded, no local PDF visual check

evidence.title: Roffe et al., Neutron-Induced Single-Event Effects on Neuromorphic Event-Based Vision Sensor
evidence.location: IEEE Access 9,85748-85763; doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2021.3085136; sectionsIII-IV, Figs 11-13; printed pp 85751,85754-85756
evidence.finding: 640 x 480 180 nm sensor, neutron beam 0.1 to>600 MeV. Observed ON bursts about 600-800 us and OFF relaxation about 8-10 ms; clusters and long tracks.
evidence.conditions: LANSCE ICE-II pulsed broad neutron spectrum, Nov 23-24 2019; dark/lit and angle tests. Beam timing contributes to measured structure.
evidence.limits: Confusion mechanism overlaps millisecond flashes. Does not supply lunar charged-particle-to-event cross-sections or validate flash filtering. Do not transport paper's speculative neutron-decay explanation.
evidence.access: full published author-hosted PDF cached; observed results reviewed

evidence.title: Sony/Prophesee IMX636 Product Brief v3.0
evidence.finding: 1280 x 720 pixels,4.86 um pitch. Area derived here 0.217678 cm 2. No radiation qualification specification found in this public brief.
evidence.conditions: Industrial event-sensor brief. Full datasheet on request. Sensor, development kit and camera assembly are distinct items.
evidence.limits: Absence of public rating is not proof of failure or absence of proprietary test data. Low-light and radiation transfer remain unknown.

evidence.title: TI TPS7H2201-SP/-SEP eFuse data sheet RevG
evidence.location: Features; section 4 Device Options; Electrical Characteristics
evidence.finding: SP rated 100 krad(Si), DSEE-free tested LET75 MeV cm²/mg. SEP grade 50 krad and LET43. 1.5-7 V, 6 A class switch. Maximum on resistance 35 mOhm at 25°C and 5 V for CFP/KGD; HTSSOP differs.
evidence.conditions: Exact ordering grade and radiation test conditions matter. EM versions not flight qualified; rating belongs to switch, not protected sensor.
evidence.limits: Not automatic downstream SEL protection. Current threshold, transient response, stored energy and restart must be sized to load. No flight rate inferred from LET threshold.
evidence.access: full data sheet cached; current grade table checked

evidence.title: Microchip RTG4 radiation-tolerant FPGAs brief
evidence.location: p 8 Features and RTG4 Product Family table
evidence.finding: TID>100 krad(Si), hardened configuration, SEL immunity claim, SECDED internal SRAM,151824 logic elements,5.2 Mbit SRAM.
evidence.conditions: Manufacturer brochure; radiation reports, order grade, timing/power and exact application design need selection. GEO solar-minimum SEU-rate example is not a lunar rate.
evidence.limits: Evidence of a feasible rad-tolerant interface/processing option, not a selected FPGA or full-board qualification. External memory, transceivers and regulators remain separate. Internal SRAM SECDED is optional and must be enabled and verified.

evidence.title: SPENVIS model service and GCR documentation
evidence.location: Home version banner; GCR model help
evidence.finding: SPENVIS4.6.14 current public banner. CREME96 solar-minimum implementation represents 1986-87 and includes anomalous cosmic rays; ISO15390 has solar-modulation inputs.
evidence.conditions: Model choice, solar epoch, geometry and confidence required. A service name alone does not define a model.
evidence.limits: Service not executed, no account created. NASA published curves used instead; their exact versions remain unknown.

evidence.title: AFRL IRENE AE9/AP9/SPM public release and User Guide
evidence.location: Home; User Guide Model Installation; documents page
evidence.finding: Electron, proton and plasma climatologies with statistical confidence including 95 th percentile. Public package Windows; Linux source by request.45 satellite datasets described on home.
evidence.conditions: Predicted percentile and duration-specific realizations require actual trajectory. Future roadmap is not proof of a released version.
evidence.limits: Not installed or run. Cannot fill 400 km/51.6 deg or 600 km/98 deg dose cells from NASA550 km/6 deg and 800 km/98 deg curves.

evidence.title: ECSS-E-ST-10-12C displacement damage expression, SPENVIS mirror
evidence.finding: Use TNID/NIEL dose, commonlyMeV/g, or explicitly referenced DDEF(particle, energy, material), e.g.10 MeV protons or 1 MeV neutrons.
evidence.conditions: NIEL integral needs differential fluence at device and material-specific displacement stopping power.
evidence.limits: TID cannot be converted into DD, nor 64 MeV proton fluence into 1 MeV neutron equivalent without NIEL weighting. No mission DD prediction here.

evidence.title: CREME-MC, How to run CREME96
evidence.location: module table: GTRN, FLUX, TRANS, LETSPEC, HUP, PUP, DOSE
evidence.finding: Separate geomagnetic transmission, shield transport, LET spectra and heavy-ion/proton rate calculations.
evidence.conditions: Rate needs compatible device response versus LET/energy and angular convention.
evidence.limits: No CREME run or selected-device rate. Integral threshold estimates in NASA Figure 8 cannot replace full rate integration.

evidence.title: NOAA Space Weather Scales
evidence.location: Solar Radiation Storms S1-S5; integral>=10 MeV flux thresholds
evidence.finding: S1=10, S3=1000, S5=100000 pfu (protons/cm 2/s/sr). These are thresholds, not guaranteed lunar storm spectra or durations.
evidence.conditions: Earth-near operational scale; anisotropy and Earth-Moon differences require care. Here isotropic incidence is an explicit sensitivity assumption.
evidence.limits: No threshold translates directly into spacecraft dose, transmitted>10 MeV flux, or false flashes. Not a real-time warning feed in this study.

evidence.title: Koontz et al., International Space Station Spacecraft Charging Environments: Modeling, Measurement, and Implications for Future Human Space Flight Programs (NASA presentation)
evidence.finding: Lunar Prospector spacecraft potentials summarized as-100 to-300 V in SPE and-40 to-80 V in geotail. Separate lunar surface values reach-4.5 kV. Magnetotail conditions a few days around full moon.
evidence.conditions: Spacecraft potential relative to plasma is not differential voltage across a specific insulator. Surface/vehicle values must stay separate.
evidence.limits: No selected-geometry charging simulation; no fixed universal lunar potential. Conduction, grounding and surface design needed independently of TID.
evidence.access: full NASA presentation cached; slide37 checked

evidence.title: NASA Small Spacecraft State of the Art, Avionics
evidence.location: section 8.2.1 Radiation Mitigation and Tolerance Schemes
evidence.finding: Separates TID, DDD, SEU, SEL; discusses hardening and fault mitigation for spacecraft avionics.
evidence.conditions: General small-spacecraft engineering guidance; individual technology ratings are device specific.
evidence.limits: Flight heritage does not qualify a selected board for lunar exposure. ECC, scrubbing and recovery need implementation verification.

evidence.title: NASA Low Earth Orbit Spacecraft Charging Design Standard
evidence.finding: LEO high-voltage systems>55 V,200-1000 km and latitude-50 to+50 deg scope.
evidence.conditions: ISS-like plasma interactions differ from auroral and lunar hot-plasma charging.
evidence.limits: Not complete lunar/polar charging guidance. Use appropriate all-environment charging practices and trajectory-specific assessment.

evidence.title: Quinn et al., Modeling shielding with PREDICCS: five solar events in2012
evidence.location: J Space Weather Space Clim 7 A 16, doi:10.1051/swsc/2017014
evidence.finding: Potential measured/model solar-event shielding validation comparator; no numeric dose taken into this analysis.
evidence.conditions: Reported comparisons include water conversions and CRaTER/RAD geometries; cannot silently relabel as silicon.
evidence.limits: Publisher PDF/HTML403 during study; excluded from quantitative dose table.
